passages.title: Our trip to the mountains
passages.text:
Last spring, our class went on a five-day trip to the mountains in Wales. We (1) ______ at a youth hostel in a small village, and every day our teachers organised a different activity. On the first morning we went climbing. I had never done it before, and at first I was too nervous to (2) ______ down, but our instructor was very patient. By lunchtime I had reached the top of the wall twice!

The next day we went on a long walk to a lake. The weather (3) ______ suddenly in the afternoon, and we got completely wet (4) ______ the way back. Luckily, the hostel staff had made hot soup for us, which warmed us up in no time.

In the evenings we played games and told stories. My best friend Leo, who is usually quite shy, (5) ______ everyone laugh with his funny impressions of our teachers. Fortunately, the teachers found them funny too!

I learnt a lot on the trip, not only about the mountains but also about working in a team. I would definitely (6) ______ it to next year's students.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: 'We stayed at a youth hostel' is the normal way to say where you slept during a trip. 'Put', 'kept' and 'spent' all need an object (you put or keep something; you spend time or money), so 'We put/kept/spent at a youth hostel' is not correct.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: When you point your eyes in a direction, the verb is 'look': 'too nervous to look down'. 'See', 'watch' and 'view' are not used with 'down' in this way.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: 'The weather changed suddenly' makes sense, and it explains why they 'got completely wet'. 'Became' and 'went' need a word after them (became cold, went grey), and weather does not 'move'.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'on the way back', meaning during the journey back to the hostel. 'In the way' has a different meaning (blocking someone), and 'at the way' and 'by the way' do not mean 'during the journey'.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: The structure is 'make someone do something': Leo 'made everyone laugh'. 'Caused' and 'got' need 'to' before the verb (caused/got everyone to laugh), and 'did everyone laugh' is not correct here.

questions.question: Choose the word that best fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: You 'recommend something to someone' when you say it is good: 'I would definitely recommend it to next year's students'. We 'advise' and 'persuade' people, not things ('advise it to' and 'persuade it to' are wrong), and 'tell it to' would mean repeating a story.
